candidates.text: The doctrine of the separation of powers was adopted by the convention of 1787, not to promote efficiency but to preclude the exercise of arbitrary power
candidates.speaker: Brandeis, dissenting
phrases: not to promote efficiency but to preclude the exercise of arbitrary power

candidates.text: The vesting of the executive power in the President was essentially a grant of the power to execute the laws
candidates.speaker: Taft
phrases: those for whom he can not continue to be responsible
those for whom he cannot continue to be responsible

candidates.text: Then there may be duties of a quasi judicial character imposed on executive officers and members of executive tribunals
candidates.speaker: Taft
phrases: duties of a quasi judicial character imposed on executive officers

candidates.text: Generally, the actual ouster of an officer is executive action; but to prescribe the conditions under which this may be done is legislative
candidates.speaker: McReynolds, dissenting
phrases: The act of hanging a criminal is executive

candidates.text: Our conclusion on the merits, sustained by the arguments before stated, is that article 2 grants to the President the executive power
candidates.speaker: Taft
